office_does: The coroner investigates sudden, violent or unexplained deaths, determines cause and manner of death, and keeps families informed.
race_blurb: Interim Coroner Alex Lathum, a Democrat appointed in September after Hayley Thompson resigned, faces Republican Derrill Fussell, who qualified as a write-in in the primary. Both say the accredited office is understaffed; the race contrasts in-office and laboratory experience with an outsider who says character and administration matter most.

candidates.summary: Interim Skagit County Coroner and former lead microbiologist at the state Public Health Laboratory who volunteered and interned in the coroner's office before his appointment.
highlights: Appointed interim coroner unanimously by commissioners in September 2026 [S3]
Pledges to respond to death scenes himself and follow national medicolegal investigation standards [S1][S4]
Would track and publish county death statistics [S1]

experience.basis: The appointed interim incumbent with prior volunteer work in the office, though his tenure as coroner is weeks long.

candidates.summary: Former flower-bulb farm manager and technology company CEO who qualified as a write-in and campaigns on protecting coroner staffing, accreditation and state reimbursements.
highlights: Qualified for the ballot with 1,197 write-in votes in the primary [S9]
Would claim every state autopsy reimbursement dollar and keep the office's IACME accreditation [S5]
Says the office is understaffed and he will lobby for full staffing [S1]

experience.basis: Has held no public office and repeatedly argues character and administrative judgment, not death-investigation experience, are the qualification.
